GAME + EMBODIED2025Nature 2025

DreamerV3

Mastering diverse control tasks through world models

Trains policies inside a learned world model with a shared algorithm configuration across diverse control tasks, connecting game and robot learning.

World modelsReinforcement learning
Details & evidence

Environment & tasks: DMLab30, including four Lasertag tasks; also Atari, Minecraft, and other environments.

Observations & actions: Task-specific observations, actions, and rewards feed an RSSM world model; actor–critic learning uses imagined trajectories. Each task is trained separately.

Scope & limitations: Fixed hyperparameters do not imply a single policy with shared weights. The DMLab aggregate is not a Lasertag score, and different interaction budgets prevent direct ranking. Compiled from existing paper notes; not independently reproduced. Original review claims are retained as source information.

Why included: Published within the five-year window; official paper page checked.

Evidence status: Official bibliographic metadata checked; experiments not independently reproduced.

Successor Feature Landmarks for Long-Horizon Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

Organizes reachable landmarks with successor features, combining graph planning and low-level goal policies for long-horizon navigation.

Planning & memoryExploration & skills
Details & evidence

Environment & tasks: Large ViZDoom visual mazes: SGM Map and Test 1/2/4/6; non-combat navigation.

Observations & actions: First-person images use pretrained SPTM representations; a high-level planner chooses landmarks and a low-level policy executes discrete navigation actions.

Scope & limitations: Separate fixed/random spawn points, difficulty levels, and maps. Training steps omit some pretraining costs; strong results on difficult tasks do not imply superiority on every task.

Why included: Published within the five-year window; official paper page checked.

Evidence status: Official bibliographic metadata checked; experiments not independently reproduced.

Original knowledge-base review label: Compiled from original notes

Publication date: 2021-12

CoSHRL

Handling Long and Richly Constrained Tasks through Constrained Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

Combines goal-conditioned skills and constrained path search to balance goal reaching against accumulated hazard costs over long tasks.

Planning & memorySafety & verification
Details & evidence

Environment & tasks: Safe ViZDoom four-leaf-clover maze with hazardous floors; non-combat navigation.

Observations & actions: The exact state and visual processing need verification. Low-level actions move in four absolute directions; the high-level policy chooses constrained subgoals.

Scope & limitations: Goal-reaching and constraint-satisfaction rates are distinct. Stochastic CVaR evidence comes from environments other than Doom. Nonzero violation rates preclude absolute safety claims; the action interface is simplified.

Why included: Published within the five-year window; official paper page checked.

Evidence status: Official bibliographic metadata checked; experiments not independently reproduced.

Exploration & skillsReinforcement learning

About the collection

A research index connecting game agents and embodied intelligence. Game research starts from the supplied Game Agent knowledge base; robotics and additional game resources come from official proceedings, research reports, and project repositories.

The organization and website layout are inspired by Awesome Robot Use Agent. This collection has its own scope, categories, and resource summaries.

Snapshot · 2026-09-14

72 unique curated resources: 6 articles, 49 papers, 5 standalone projects, 4 datasets, 8 benchmarks or environments, and 8 video demonstrations. Dataset and benchmark papers appear in multiple views, so these counts overlap. 8 candidates are listed separately.

Selection criteria

TrackPublication windowSelection basis
Leading conferences & journals14 Sep 2021 – 14 Sep 2026Relevant main-conference papers and journal articles with official publication records. Priority venues include NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, AAAI, IJCAI, RSS, CoRL, ICRA, IROS, Nature, Science, T-RO, IJRR, TPAMI, JMLR, and TMLR.
Selected arXiv research14 Sep 2025 – 14 Sep 2026First submission date, with a specific editorial rationale and supporting sources. Evidence can include systematic evaluations, released models or environments, and substantial research reports. No citation ranking is claimed.
Tools & environmentsReviewed for current research useStandalone infrastructure is assessed by purpose, interface, and setup requirements. The paper publication window does not apply.

This venue list reflects the collection's subject-specific editorial policy, rather than a single official ranking. Workshops and unconfirmed submissions are distinguished from main-conference publications. See the full collection policy.

Sources and verification

The source table contained 106 rows. Removing 19 untitled rows and merging 4 duplicates produced 83 distinct titled leads. Historical counts on the knowledge-base homepage were not used for this snapshot.

Checks primarily cover bibliographic records, project descriptions, and abstracts. Original knowledge-base review labels are retained as source claims, translated into English. They do not represent a fresh full-text review or independent experiment reproduction.

Action abstractionKeyboard/mouse, program APIs, or skillsJoints, end-effector poses, or navigation/manipulation skills
Data & learningPlayer traces, online interaction, video pretrainingDemonstrations, teleoperation, simulation, real interaction
Execution constraintsDecision latency, frame rate, paused executionControl frequency, collisions, hardware limits
EvaluationMap splits, task metrics, samples, and seedsTask success, generalization, and human intervention

Shared methods do not by themselves establish transfer between domains. Frame generation, game navigation, robot planning, and physical execution retain their respective evidence boundaries.

Video demonstrations

The video gallery embeds original research-team videos, with source links, credits, and related work. Game control, generated frames, real robots, and simulation are labeled separately. Selected clips illustrate behavior; they do not replace benchmark evaluations. Videos load as you approach them and play only when requested. If an external host is unavailable, use the source link on the card.

Maintenance and contributions

The README and website share the same catalogue. This is a manually curated snapshot. Additions should include official sources and satisfy the selection criteria. Read the contribution guide or visit the GitHub repository.
